newsitem.title: USA: Williams buys Conoco terminal stakes.
newsitem.headline: Williams buys Conoco terminal stakes.

text.p: Williams Energy Ventures said Tuesday it has purchased Conoco Inc.'s 45.5 percent stake in eight petroleum products terminals in the Southeast.
The price the Williams Cos. Inc. subsidiary paid the DuPont Co. subsidiary was not disclosed.
The terminals, with a combined storage capacity of 1.5 million barrels, receive oil products from Gulf Coast refineries via Colonial Pipe Line and Plantation Pipe Line.
The terminals are in Montvale and Richmond, Va.; Charlotte, Greensboro and Selma, N.C.; North Augusta, S.C.; Albany, Ga.; and Nashville, Tenn.
Murphy Oil Corp. USA owns 20.5 percent of the terminals, while TOC Terminals, a subsidiary of Stratus Petroleum Corp., owns 34 percent.
Williams said Conoco will retain its ownership stake in seven terminals including Spartanburg, S.C.; Doraville and Macon, Ga.; Knoxville and Chattanooga, Tenn.; and Birmingham and Montgomery, Ala.
Houston-based Conoco has 16,000 employees and operates in 30 countries.
Tulsa, Okla.-based Williams Co. owns energy and business communications companies.
